correctness.rationale: The Pell arithmetic lemma itself is correct: for m nearest sqrt(3)n the nonzero integer m²-3n² implies liminf n||sqrt(3)n||≥1/(2sqrt(3)), with equality on both parity classes of Pell denominators. However the claimed quantum-graph band-width limsup does not follow from the submitted asymptotic citation without a uniform error estimate in the singular near-resonant regime. Along Pell denominators |sin(pi sqrt(3)n)|~const/n, the nominal csc factor grows like n and the putative width is O(1), while the original high-energy local band-edge expansion was derived by treating resonances as isolated and small perturbations. Nearby resonance families can collide at the same n^-1 wave-number scale; terms suppressed for fixed nonresonant phases may contribute at leading order. No actual Floquet determinant estimate uniform in n at |sin|~1/n or coupled-resonance reanalysis is supplied. Merely copying a pointwise/formal O(n^-2) remainder as though uniform over these singular denominators does not certify the spectral limsup. This is a motivated missing scientific lemma, not failure of Pell mathematics or a finite numerical discrepancy.
